details:
Q1: Where should the fix go, given that `gh_retry`'s comment (`scripts/gh_helpers.sh:1196-1198`) promises "If the successful attempt's output cannot be delivered (the reader closed the pipe), the copy's non-zero status is returned and the command is not re-run", and that promise is currently broken on ubuntu-26.04 runners?
Choices:
- A: Fix the helper. Change the successful-attempt copy in `gh_retry`, and the matching copy in `gh_retry_to_file` if it has the same problem, so that an undelivered output returns non-zero whichever coreutils is installed. Keep the documented contract and the test's `rc != 0` assertion as they are. Planning picks the copy method. (RECOMMENDED)
- B: Fix only the test. Leave `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` unchanged, change the test to require only that the command is not re-run (`_calls == 1`), and accept `rc=0` when `cat` is uutils. The non-zero-status part of the comment would be reworded as best-effort. This is a smaller change but weakens what the contract guarantees in production.
Sources:
- [uutils/coreutils #8919: SIGPIPE handling is missing in many utilities](https://github.com/uutils/coreutils/issues/8919)
- [safeinsights/canopycms #1106: uutils cat reported 0 with input unread (Ubuntu 26.04)](https://github.com/safeinsights/canopycms/issues/1106)
- [FRIKKern/barkpark PR #25075: pipefail self-test uses GNU cat when the box's cat is uutils](https://github.com/FRIKKern/barkpark/pull/25075)
- [michakraus/ResearchHarness PR #81: stub's large diff dies of SIGPIPE without GNU cat](https://github.com/michakraus/ResearchHarness/pull/81)
